runbook.description: when one or more instances of a deployment are down (the 'down' count is greater than zero)
runbook.resolution: scale the affected deployment to zero replicas then scale it back to its original instance count, this forces the scheduler to reschedule pods and bring all instances up cleanly on healthy nodes

runbook.description: when service logs show 'connection pool exhausted' or 'no available connections' to a database
runbook.resolution: increase the database connection pool size (maxPoolSize) for that service in its config map, roll-restart the affected instances so they pick up the new pool size, then confirm pool utilisation stays below 80 percent under load

runbook.description: when a deployment qps is above its qpsthreshold, meaning the service is receiving more traffic than it is provisioned for
runbook.resolution: enable request rate limiting at the ingress or api gateway for that service and trigger horizontal autoscaling to add replicas until qps-per-instance falls back below the threshold

runbook.description: when a deployment fps (failures per second) is above its fpsthreshold
runbook.resolution: identify the immediate downstream dependency named in the service logs (database or upstream api), if that dependency is unhealthy open a circuit breaker to shed load and protect it while it recovers, then remediate the dependency

runbook.description: when logs show repeated database write failures or write timeouts that persist after automatic retries
runbook.resolution: confirm the database is accepting writes and is not in read-only or failover state, if the database is healthy increase the write timeout and connection pool for the service, if the database itself is degraded escalate to the database on-call team

runbook.description: when instances are OOMKilled (killed for exceeding their memory limit) due to backlogged request buffers under load
runbook.resolution: treat OOMKills as a symptom of upstream overload, first relieve the load (rate limit and fix the root dependency), only if memory pressure persists after load is normal should you raise the deployment memory limit and restart it

runbook.description: when a service reports a circuit breaker in the OPEN state for a dependency
runbook.resolution: leave the breaker open until the dependency recovers (it protects the dependency from a thundering herd), fix the underlying dependency, then let the breaker half-open and close automatically as success rate recovers

runbook.description: when instances fail readiness probes due to node disk pressure (node reporting DiskPressure)
runbook.resolution: cordon and drain the affected node so pods reschedule onto healthy nodes, then reclaim disk on the bad node by clearing evicted pods, old container images and logs before uncordoning it

runbook.description: when a service starts degrading immediately after a new version was deployed, especially memory climbing steadily with no change in traffic (a regression)
runbook.resolution: roll back the deployment to the previous known-good version to restore service quickly, then reproduce and debug the regression in a non-production environment before re-releasing

runbook.description: when the failing dependency is an EXTERNAL third-party service and its own status page confirms an outage (the internal service is otherwise healthy)
runbook.resolution: do not attempt an internal code fix, keep the circuit breaker open, queue and retry the affected work where possible, and escalate to the vendor while monitoring their status page for recovery

runbook.description: when a cache outage (redis or memcached unreachable) causes a stampede of traffic onto the database, seen as cache hit ratio dropping to near zero and database qps spiking
runbook.resolution: restore or fail over the cache, temporarily rate-limit or shed read traffic to protect the overloaded database, then warm the cache back up before removing the rate limit
